questions.questionText: What is the most accurate and precise method to measure the thickness of a coin?

options.text: Use a micrometer screw gauge.
Use a ruler and look at the scale perpendicularly.
Use a top pan balance.
Use the displacement method with water in a measuring cylinder.

questions.questionText:
A skydiver reaches terminal velocity. Then he opens his parachute.
What happens to the skydiver as the parachute opens?

options.text: There is a decrease in weight.
There is acceleration upwards.
There is an increase in speed.
There is movement upwards.

questions.questionText:
A piece of steel is taken from the Earth to the Moon for an experiment. The gravitational field
strength on the Moon is smaller than on the Earth.
Which statement about the piece of steel is correct?

options.text: It has less mass on the Moon than on the Earth.
It has more mass on the Moon than on the Earth.
It weighs less on the Moon than on the Earth.
It weighs more on the Moon than on the Earth.

questions.questionText:
A boat is travelling at a steady speed in a straight line across the surface of a lake.
Which statement about the boat is correct?

options.text: The resultant force on the boat is in the direction of motion.
The resultant force on the boat is in the opposite direction to its motion.
The resultant force on the boat is vertically downwards.
The resultant force on the boat is zero.

questions.questionText:
A box of mass m slides down a slope of length l and vertical height d against a frictional force F.
mass m
stop
As the box slides down the slope, it loses gravitational potential energy and it does work against
the friction.
Which row gives the loss in gravitational potential energy and the work done against friction?
loss in gravitational work done
potential energy against friction

options.text: mgd Fl
mgd Fd
mgl Fl
mgl Fd

questions.questionText:

useful
input output energy
energy
wasted
output energy
The device is 50% efficient.
Which equation is correct?

options.text: input energy = useful output energy ÷ 2
useful output energy = wasted output energy ÷ 2
wasted output energy = useful output energy
wasted output energy = useful output energy ÷ 2

questions.questionText:
Brownian motion is observed when using a microscope to look at smoke particles in air.
What causes the smoke particles to move at random?

options.text: Smoke particles are hit by air molecules.
Smoke particles are moved by convection currents in the air.
Smoke particles have different weights and fall at different speeds.
Smoke particles hit the walls of the container.

questions.questionText:
Gas molecules striking a container wall cause a pressure to be exerted on the wall.
Which statement explains this?

options.text: When a molecule rebounds there must be a change in its energy.
When a molecule rebounds there must be a change in its momentum.
When a molecule rebounds there must be a change in its speed.
When a molecule rebounds there must be a change in its temperature.

questions.questionText:
Equal masses of two different liquids are put into identical beakers.
Liquid 1 is heated for 100s and liquid 2 is heated for 200s by heaters of the same power.
Each liquid has the same rise in temperature.
different liquids
of same mass
liquid 1 liquid 2
heating time = 100 s heating time = 200 s
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Each beaker of liquid has the same thermal capacity.
Each beaker of liquid receives the same energy.
Liquid 1 receives more energy than liquid 2.
The thermal capacity of liquid 1 is less than the thermal capacity of liquid 2.

questions.questionText:
A copper bar and a wooden bar are joined. A piece of paper is wrapped tightly around the join.
The bar is heated strongly at the centre for a short time, and the paper goes brown on one side
only.
wood paper copper
heat
Which side goes brown, and what does this show about wood and copper?
brown side wood copper

options.text: copper conductor insulator
copper insulator conductor
wood conductor insulator
wood insulator conductor

questions.questionText:
A converging lens is used as a magnifying glass to view an object.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The image is inverted.
The image is nearer the lens than the object.
The image is the same size.
The image is virtual.

questions.questionText:
Light travels in a vacuum and then enters a glass block. The speed of the light in the glass block
is 2.0 × 108m/s.
Which statement about the speed of light is correct?

options.text: The speed in a vacuum is 1.5 times the speed in the glass.
The speed in the glass is the same as the speed in a vacuum.
The speed in the glass is 1.5 times the speed in a vacuum.
The speed in the glass is 1.0 × 108 times the speed in a vacuum.

questions.questionText:
A fire alarm is not loud enough and the pitch is too low. An engineer adjusts the alarm so that it
produces a louder note of a higher pitch.
What effect does this have on the amplitude and on the frequency of the sound?
amplitude frequency

options.text: larger greater
larger smaller
smaller greater
smaller smaller

questions.questionText:
In a child’s toy, metal fish are lifted out of a toy pond using a metal rod. The fish are magnetically
attracted to the end of the rod. There is no magnetic force between the fish themselves.
metal rod
toy pond
metal fish
What are possible materials from which the fish and the rod are made?
fish rod

options.text: aluminium soft iron
aluminium steel
soft iron soft iron
soft iron steel

questions.questionText: What is the most effective method of demagnetising a bar magnet?

options.text: placing the magnet in a solenoid carrying a large alternating current and gradually decreasing the current
placing the magnet in a solenoid carrying a large direct current and gradually decreasing the current
placing the magnet in a solenoid that produces a magnetic field in the opposite direction to the magnet
placing the magnet next to an identical bar magnet with its poles in the opposite direction

questions.questionText:
A magnet near a coil of wire is attracted to the coil only when there is a current in the coil.
Which statement explains this force of attraction?

options.text: The coil of wire has its own gravitational field.
The coil of wire is made from soft iron.
The current in the coil of wire creates a magnetic field.
The current in the coil of wire induces a charge on the magnet.

questions.questionText:
A student rubs a plastic rod with a cloth.
The rod becomes positively charged.
What has happened to the rod?

options.text: It has gained electrons.
It has gained protons.
It has lost electrons.
It has lost protons.

questions.questionText: Which quantity is measured in coulombs?

options.text: charge
current
electromotive force
power

questions.questionText:
A student connects a variable potential divider (potentiometer) circuit.
T V
12V
What happens to the reading on the voltmeter as the sliding terminal T is moved from R to S?

options.text: It decreases from 12V to 0V.
It increases from 0V to 12V.
It remains at 0V.
It remains at 12V.

questions.questionText:
A light-dependent resistor (LDR) and a resistor R are connected in a series circuit. Light falls on
the LDR.
The brightness of the light falling on the LDR decreases.
What happens to the resistance of the LDR and what happens to the reading on the ammeter?
resistance reading on
of LDR ammeter

options.text: decreases decreases
decreases increases
increases decreases
increases increases

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a logic gate.
Which input combinations at P and Q gives an output of 0 at R?
P Q

A simple d.c. electric motor is fitted with a coil that rotates in a magnetic field. A commutator
connects the power supply to the coil.
What is the purpose of the commutator?

options.text: It converts a.c. into d.c. in the coil.
It prevents the current from becoming too great, because the coil has a low resistance.
It reverses the direction of the current in the coil after every 180° rotation of the coil.
It switches the current off momentarily after every 90° rotation of the coil.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a relay?

options.text: to change a large voltage into a small voltage
to change a small voltage into a large voltage
to use a large current to switch on a small current
to use a small current to switch on a large current

questions.questionText:
Which row gives the relative charge of an electron, a neutron and a proton?
electron neutron proton

A nuclide of element X undergoes β-decay.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The nucleon number increases by 1.
The nucleon number stays the same.
The product is another nuclide of an isotope of X.
The proton number decreases by 1.

questions.questionText:
A sample of radioactive isotope is decaying.
The nuclei of which atoms will decay first?

options.text: It is impossible to know because radioactive decay is random.
It is impossible to know unless the age of the material is known.
The atoms near the centre will decay first because they are surrounded by more atoms.
The atoms near the surface will decay first because the radiation can escape more easily.
